1. Overview

The GBL Admin & Supervisor Dashboard is the central monitoring console for the Generating Better Livelihoods (GBL) Programme. It provides Administrators and Supervisors with real-time visibility into programme indicators spanning participant enrollment, social interventions, livelihood activities, coaching performance, dropout trends, and outcome measurements.

The dashboard is organised into two major indicator streams — Output Indicators (tracking activity-level delivery) and Outcome Indicators (tracking participant-level change) — plus a suite of management tools for templates, forms, surveys, and audit logs.

Both Admins and Supervisors can access all dashboard views. Administrative functions such as template deactivation and audit log review are available to Admins only.

2. Dashboard Navigation

When you first open the GBL Admin Dashboard you are presented with the Indicator Type Selection screen — the entry point to all monitoring data. From here you choose whether to explore Output Indicators or Outcome Indicators.

Dashboard Home — Indicator Type Selection (Output vs Outcome)

Two-Path Navigation

The dashboard follows a consistent three-level drill-down pattern for both indicator streams:

StreamLevel 1Level 2Level 3
Output IndicatorsSelect "Output Indicators"Choose from 8 topics (e.g. Coaching)View Snapshot / Graphs tabs
Outcome IndicatorsSelect "Outcome Indicators"Choose Cumulative or Individual, then one of 6 topicsView detailed metric breakdown
Indicator Types Selection Screen

Breadcrumb Navigation

Every detail screen displays a breadcrumb trail at the top of the page, showing your current location within the navigation hierarchy (e.g. Dashboard > Output Indicators > Coaching). Click any breadcrumb item to navigate back to that level without losing your current filter selections. This allows you to quickly switch between topics while keeping your Cohort Year and provincial filters active.

Output Indicators — 8 Topics List
Tip: Use the breadcrumb trail rather than the browser back button to preserve your active filter context when moving between sections.

3. Filters & Cohort Year

All dashboard views share a common filter bar that allows you to narrow the data to the exact cohort, geography, and time period you need. Filters are applied globally to every metric on the current screen and persist as you navigate between topics within the same session.

Available Filters

FilterLocationPurposeExample Value
Cohort YearTop header selectorSelects the programme cohort year. All data displayed is scoped to this year. Must be set correctly before reviewing any metrics.2026
Enrollment DateFilter bar (dropdown)Specifies the date type to use for filtering — e.g. date of enrollment, date of consent, SLA signing date.Enrollment Date
From DateFilter bar (calendar picker)Start of the date range for the selected date type. Leave blank for all records from the beginning of the cohort.01 Jan 2026
To DateFilter bar (calendar picker)End of the date range. Leave blank to include records up to today.31 Mar 2026
All ProvincesFilter bar (dropdown)Scope data to a specific South African province. Defaults to all provinces.Gauteng
All DistrictsFilter bar (dropdown)Further refine within a selected province to a specific district municipality. Only available after selecting a province.City of Tshwane
All Linkage ChampionsFilter bar (dropdown)Filter data by a specific Linkage Champion (LC). Useful for supervisors reviewing individual LC performance.LC Name
All GendersFilter bar (dropdown)Filter participant data by gender to analyse gender-disaggregated indicators.Female
Important: Always verify the Cohort Year selector before reviewing data. If the wrong year is selected, all metrics displayed will reflect incorrect cohort data.
Note: Filter selections are shared across all Output Indicator topics. When you switch from one topic (e.g. Coaching) to another (e.g. Dropouts), your filter selections remain active.

4. Participant Enrollment & Targeting

The Participant Enrollment & Targeting section tracks the full onboarding pipeline — from initial CSG list assignment through to SLA signing and programme enrolment. It provides supervisors with a real-time view of how many eligible participants have been contacted, profiled, consented, and formally enrolled, enabling early identification of bottlenecks in the intake process.

Snapshot Tab

Participant Enrollment & Targeting — Snapshot Tab

Key Metrics (Snapshot)

MetricDescription
Assigned (CSG Lists)Total number of participants assigned from the SASSA CSG lists for the selected cohort year and filters.
Contacted by LC/LF %Percentage of assigned participants who have been contacted by a Linkage Champion or Linkage Facilitator.
Consent & Profiled %Percentage of assigned participants who have given informed consent and completed their participant profile.
SLA Signed %Percentage of profiled participants who have signed the Service Level Agreement, confirming formal enrolment.
TargetedCount of participants identified as high-priority for additional targeting interventions.
EnrolledTotal participants with a completed SLA and active enrolment status.
Male / Female SplitGender disaggregation of enrolled participants across the filtered geography.
Province / District BreakdownDrill-down counts by province and district for enrolled participants.

Graphs Tab

The Graphs tab visualises enrollment pipeline metrics as trend charts over the selected date range, enabling supervisors to identify patterns such as seasonal intake peaks, slow-down periods, or the impact of outreach drives on contact and consent rates.

Participant Enrollment & Targeting — Graphs Tab (Trend Charts)
Tip: Use the Snapshot tab for current totals and the Graphs tab to identify trends. If the Contacted % is high but Consent % is low, investigate outreach quality rather than reach.

5. Social Protection Referrals

The Social Protection Referrals section tracks the referral of GBL participants to social protection programmes and services beyond the core GBL intervention — including government grants, social welfare services, healthcare, and legal aid. It monitors both the volume of referrals made and the proportion of participants who successfully accessed the referred service, providing insight into the effectiveness of the programme's social safety-net linkages.

Social Protection Referrals — Snapshot

Key Metrics (Snapshot)

MetricDescription
Total Referrals MadeCumulative number of referrals recorded for participants in the filtered cohort and geography.
% ReferredProportion of enrolled participants for whom at least one social protection referral has been completed.
Referrals CompletedCount of referrals where the participant confirmed access to or uptake of the referred service.
Referral Type BreakdownDistribution of referrals by category (e.g. healthcare, legal, social welfare, grants).
Pending ReferralsReferrals recorded but not yet confirmed as completed — flagged for follow-up by the LC.
Note: The Graphs tab shows referral trend lines over time, useful for monitoring whether referral activity aligns with programme delivery phases.

6. Social Empowerment

The Social Empowerment section monitors community integration activities and psychosocial support interventions delivered to GBL participants. It captures participation in group activities, community forums, and support sessions designed to build participants' confidence, social networks, and sense of agency. This data helps supervisors ensure that the social dimensions of livelihoods development are being addressed alongside economic and financial activities.

Social Empowerment — Snapshot

Key Metrics (Snapshot)

MetricDescription
Participants EngagedTotal participants who have attended at least one Social Empowerment session or activity.
% of Enrolled ReachedSocial Empowerment reach as a proportion of the enrolled participant base.
Sessions ConductedTotal social empowerment sessions held in the filtered period and geography.
Group vs. Individual SessionsSplit between group-based activities and one-on-one psychosocial support interactions.
Topics CoveredBreakdown of session themes (e.g. self-esteem, community integration, gender-based violence awareness).
Tip: Use the province/district filter to identify areas where Social Empowerment engagement is below target and follow up with the local LC team.

7. Big Push

The Big Push section tracks intensive, time-bound support activities that are delivered to participants at key programme milestones. Big Push activities represent concentrated bursts of intervention — combining multiple programme components (financial training, market linkages, asset transfers, and coaching) within a defined period. Monitoring Big Push delivery ensures that high-intensity support reaches the intended participants on schedule.

Big Push — Snapshot

Key Metrics (Snapshot)

MetricDescription
Big Push EligibleNumber of participants who meet the criteria to receive Big Push support in the current cohort.
Big Push ReceivedCount of participants who have completed at least one Big Push activity.
% CoveredBig Push coverage as a proportion of eligible participants.
Activity Type BreakdownDistribution of Big Push activities by type (e.g. asset transfer, market linkage, financial literacy).
Average Activities per ParticipantMean number of Big Push activities completed per participant who has been reached.
Note: Big Push coverage gaps (low % Covered) should be escalated promptly as these activities are time-sensitive within the programme cycle.

8. Livelihood Promotion

The Livelihood Promotion section monitors livelihood activities and interventions delivered to participants — including enterprise development training, market linkage support, business mentoring, and skills development. It tracks both activity delivery (how many sessions have been conducted) and participant uptake (how many participants have engaged with livelihood support), providing a comprehensive view of livelihood service delivery performance across geographies.

Livelihood Promotion — Snapshot

Key Metrics (Snapshot)

MetricDescription
Participants ReachedTotal participants who have received at least one livelihood promotion activity.
% of EnrolledLivelihood Promotion reach as a proportion of the enrolled participant pool.
Activities DeliveredTotal livelihood activities completed across all types in the filtered period.
Activity Type DistributionBreakdown by activity category (enterprise development, skills training, market linkage, mentoring).
Completion RateProportion of started activities that were completed (vs. dropped or incomplete).
District CoverageNumber of districts where at least one livelihood activity has been delivered.
Tip: Compare Livelihood Promotion reach % with Coaching visit frequency to ensure participants receiving livelihood support are also receiving adequate follow-up coaching.

9. Financial Inclusion

The Financial Inclusion section tracks participant access to and uptake of formal financial services and products. This includes opening bank accounts, accessing credit or savings products, obtaining insurance, and completing financial literacy training. Financial inclusion metrics are a key indicator of participants' progress towards economic independence and sustainable livelihoods.

Financial Inclusion — Snapshot

Key Metrics (Snapshot)

MetricDescription
Bank Accounts OpenedNumber of participants who have opened a formal bank account during the programme.
Financial Literacy TrainingCount and percentage of participants who have completed at least one financial literacy session.
Savings Product AccessParticipants who have opened or are actively using a formal savings product.
Credit AccessParticipants who have successfully accessed a formal credit product (loan, micro-finance).
Insurance UptakeParticipants with at least one active insurance product (e.g. funeral cover, health insurance).
% Financially IncludedOverall financial inclusion rate — participants with two or more financial products as a proportion of enrolled participants.
Note: Use the gender filter to monitor financial inclusion gaps between male and female participants — a key equity indicator for the GBL programme.

10. Coaching

The Coaching section provides supervisors with a detailed view of coaching session delivery, visit frequency, and Linkage Champion (LC) performance. Regular coaching is one of the most critical programme components — it reinforces skills, supports goal-setting, and maintains participant motivation. This section allows supervisors to identify LCs with low visit rates, participants not receiving adequate coaching, and trends in session quality over time.

Coaching — Snapshot

Key Metrics (Snapshot)

MetricDescription
Total Sessions ConductedCumulative coaching sessions logged by all LCs in the filtered period and geography.
Participants CoachedNumber of unique participants who have received at least one coaching visit.
Average Visits per ParticipantMean number of coaching sessions per participant — a key quality indicator. Target is typically ≥4 visits per quarter.
% Participants Meeting Visit TargetProportion of participants who have received the minimum required number of visits in the period.
LC PerformanceVisit counts per Linkage Champion — identify high and low performers across the filtered geography.
Visit Frequency DistributionBreakdown of participants by number of visits received (e.g. 0 visits, 1–2 visits, 3–4 visits, 5+ visits).
Tip: Filter by individual LC to review their coaching caseload. If visit counts are low, check whether the issue is caseload size, geographic access, or data capture gaps.

11. Drop Outs

The Drop Outs section tracks participant attrition — monitoring who has left the programme, when they left, why they left, and where dropout rates are highest. Understanding dropout patterns is essential for programme quality improvement: high dropout rates in specific districts, demographics, or programme phases indicate areas requiring targeted intervention. This section also supports retention analytics by identifying at-risk participant segments before formal dropout occurs.

Drop Outs — Snapshot

Key Metrics (Snapshot)

MetricDescription
Total DropoutsCumulative count of participants who have formally exited the programme in the filtered cohort year.
Dropout Rate %Dropouts as a percentage of enrolled participants — the primary retention indicator.
Dropout Reasons BreakdownDistribution of recorded dropout reasons (e.g. relocation, death, employment, personal circumstances, programme dissatisfaction).
Dropout by Programme PhaseIdentifies at which stage of the programme most dropouts occur — early phase dropouts may indicate onboarding issues.
Dropout by District / ProvinceGeographic distribution of dropouts — highlights areas with disproportionate attrition.
Dropout by GenderGender disaggregation of dropout counts — important for identifying equity concerns in retention.
Month-on-Month TrendAvailable on the Graphs tab — shows whether dropout rates are increasing, decreasing, or stable over time.
Alert: If the Dropout Rate % exceeds programme targets, use province and district filters to localise the issue and escalate to the relevant field team immediately.

12. Outcome Indicators – Overview

Outcome Indicators measure the impact of the GBL programme at the participant level — capturing changes in income, assets, savings, financial behaviour, and social empowerment over time. While Output Indicators track what was delivered, Outcome Indicators track what changed for participants as a result of programme participation.

Outcome data is typically collected through structured assessments, surveys, and periodic measurement tools — separate from the activity logs that feed Output Indicators. The GBL platform organises Outcome Indicators into two sub-types, each with 6 topics, giving 12 outcome topic areas in total.

Outcome Indicators — Cumulative vs Individual Selection

Two Sub-Types Explained

Sub-TypeUnit of MeasurementPurposeTopics
Cumulative IndicatorsHousehold & Participant (aggregate)Tracks cumulative change across the household or participant group — ideal for measuring collective progress and programme-level impact.6 topics
Individual IndicatorsIndividual ParticipantTracks changes at the individual participant level — enabling personalised progress monitoring and identification of participants who need additional support.6 topics
Note: Both sub-types cover the same 6 thematic areas (Income, Assets, Savings, Record Keeping, Debt/Credit, Social Empowerment & Dignity), but are measured and aggregated differently.

13. Cumulative Indicators

Cumulative Indicators aggregate outcome data at the household and participant-group level, providing a programme-wide view of collective change. These indicators are used in programme reporting, donor submissions, and strategic planning. Each of the 6 cumulative topics has its own dedicated detail view accessible from the topic list.

Cumulative Indicators — 6 Topics

The 6 Cumulative Indicator Topics

#TopicWhat It Measures
1Income by Household and ParticipantChanges in household and individual income levels over the programme period. Tracks income sources, amounts, and growth across cohorts.
2Asset Accumulation by Household and ParticipantGrowth in physical and productive asset ownership — livestock, equipment, household goods, and business assets.
3SavingsParticipation in savings groups and formal savings products; changes in saving behaviour and accumulated savings balances.
4Record KeepingAdoption of business and household record keeping practices — a proxy for financial management capability development.
5Debt/CreditAccess to and responsible use of formal credit; changes in debt levels and borrowing behaviour over the programme period.
6Social Empowerment & DignitySelf-reported measures of empowerment, agency, decision-making, and community standing — captured through validated psychosocial tools.

Detail View Example — Income by Household

Clicking on any cumulative topic opens a detailed breakdown view. The example below shows the Income by Household and Participant detail screen, illustrating the level of granularity available for outcome data analysis.

Outcome Detail — Income by Household and Participant
Tip: Use the Cohort Year and date range filters before opening any Cumulative Indicator topic to ensure you are viewing the correct measurement period data.

14. Individual Indicators

Individual Indicators track outcome changes at the level of each individual participant, enabling programme staff to monitor personal progress, identify participants who are falling behind, and tailor support accordingly. The 6 thematic areas mirror those of the Cumulative Indicators but are measured and presented per participant rather than as household or group aggregates.

Individual Indicators — 6 Topics

The 6 Individual Indicator Topics

#TopicWhat It Measures
1IncomeIndividual participant income changes — sources, amounts, and progression over the programme cycle.
2Asset AccumulationIndividual asset ownership and growth — productive and household assets acquired during the programme.
3SavingsIndividual saving behaviour, amounts saved, and product use at the personal level.
4Record KeepingIndividual adoption and consistency of record keeping practices.
5Debt/CreditIndividual credit access, debt levels, and responsible credit use tracked per participant.
6Social Empowerment & DignityIndividual psychosocial outcome scores — self-esteem, agency, and empowerment measures for each participant.
Note: Individual Indicators share the same navigation structure as Cumulative Indicators. Select a topic from the list to access its detail view with participant-level breakdowns. Filter by LC or district to review performance within your supervisory scope.
Tip: Use Individual Indicators to identify specific participants who show no improvement across multiple outcome areas — these participants may need escalated coaching or additional referrals.

15. Template Management

The Template Management section is the administrative hub for managing IDP (Individual Development Plan) templates used across the GBL programme. Templates define the structured goal-setting and task frameworks that LCs use when working with participants. They are uploaded via CSV and managed centrally by Administrators — ensuring all field teams are working from approved, current template versions.

Template Library

Template Management — Library List

Template Fields

FieldDescription
Template NameThe unique name of the IDP template as uploaded.
StatusActive or Inactive. Active templates are available for use by LCs; Inactive templates are archived.
CreatorThe Admin user who uploaded the template.
Tasks CountNumber of tasks/goals defined within the template.
Created DateDate and time the template was uploaded to the platform.
ActionsAvailable actions for the template (see below).

Template Actions

Template Management — Actions Dropdown
ActionWhat It Does
ViewOpens the template in read-only mode. The Template Library is view-only after creation — templates cannot be edited after upload. To update a template, deactivate the old version and upload a new CSV.
DeactivateMarks the template as Inactive, removing it from LC selection screens. Deactivated templates remain in the library for audit and reference purposes. Export the template as CSV before deactivating.
Export as CSVDownloads the template definition as a CSV file. Use this to create modified versions of existing templates for re-upload.

How to Upload a New Template

  1. Click the Download Sample CSV button to obtain the correct template format.
  2. Open the sample CSV and fill in your template name, tasks, goal categories, and target values.
  3. Save the completed CSV file.
  4. Click Upload Template (CSV) and select your file.
  5. Confirm the upload — the new template will appear in the library with Status: Active.
Important: Templates cannot be edited after upload. If a template needs changes, export it as CSV, make your edits, deactivate the old version, and upload the updated file as a new template.

16. Forms & Surveys Management

The Forms and Surveys Management section provides Administrators with centralised control over the programme's data collection instruments — including intake forms, consent forms, profiling questionnaires, outcome measurement surveys, and monitoring checklists. This section allows Admins to view, manage, and maintain the forms used by field staff and participants throughout the programme lifecycle.

Forms and Surveys Management

Key Functions

FunctionDescription
View FormsBrowse the library of all active forms and surveys available within the platform.
Form StatusMonitor which forms are active and which are archived — ensure only current versions are in use.
Survey ManagementManage periodic outcome surveys, including setting availability windows and linking surveys to specific cohorts.
Response TrackingView submission counts and completion rates for active surveys and forms.
Note: Only Administrators have access to the Forms and Surveys Management section. Supervisors wishing to review form submission data should request reports from their Administrator.

17. Audit Log

The Audit Log provides a complete, tamper-evident record of all significant actions performed within the GBL platform — including data modifications, template uploads, user management actions, form submissions, and system configuration changes. It is a critical tool for accountability, compliance, and investigation of data discrepancies. The Audit Log is read-only and cannot be edited or deleted.

Audit Log

What the Audit Log Tracks

Entry FieldDescription
TimestampDate and time the action was performed, recorded in the system's server time.
UserThe platform user (Admin, Supervisor, LC) who performed the action.
Action TypeCategory of action (e.g. Create, Update, Delete, Upload, Login, Export).
ModuleThe platform module where the action occurred (e.g. Templates, Participants, Forms, Users).
DescriptionHuman-readable description of the specific action taken and the records affected.
IP AddressNetwork address from which the action was performed — used for security investigations.

Using the Audit Log for Compliance

  1. Use the date range filter to scope the log to a specific review period.
  2. Filter by User to review all actions performed by a specific team member.
  3. Filter by Action Type (e.g. Delete, Export) to identify high-risk operations.
  4. Cross-reference Audit Log entries with Dashboard data to investigate unexplained metric changes.
  5. Export the filtered log for inclusion in compliance reports or incident investigations.
Compliance Note: The Audit Log must be reviewed regularly by Administrators as part of the programme's data governance obligations. Unusual activity (e.g. bulk deletions, off-hours logins) should be escalated to the programme Data Manager.

18. Tips & Best Practices

Set the Cohort Year first: Always select the correct Cohort Year in the header selector before reviewing any data. The dashboard defaults to the current year — if you are reviewing historical data, change this before opening any indicator section.
Use geographic filters strategically: Use the Province and District filters to scope data to your specific area of responsibility. Supervisors should always filter to their assigned district before sharing metrics in team meetings or reports.
Navigate with breadcrumbs: Use the breadcrumb trail at the top of each screen to navigate back between levels. This preserves your active filter selections, whereas using the browser back button may reset filters.
Snapshot vs. Graphs: The Snapshot tab provides current-period totals and is the best view for reporting numbers at a point in time. The Graphs tab shows trends over time and is best for performance monitoring, identifying seasonal patterns, and tracking improvement over the programme cycle.
Export before deactivating templates: Always use Export as CSV to download a copy of a template before deactivating it. Deactivated templates cannot be restored to Active status — a new upload is required if the template is needed again.
Audit Log hygiene: Review the Audit Log at least monthly to identify any unusual system activity. Set up a regular calendar reminder to check for bulk data changes, exports, or deletions performed outside of business hours.
